newsitem.title: CHINA: China lead exports around 200,000T in 1996 - analyst.
newsitem.headline: China lead exports around 200,000T in 1996 - analyst.

text.p: Chinese exports of lead and lead alloys could reach 200,000 tonnes in 1996, with imports expected to be around 10,000 tonnes, a China National Nonferrous Metals Industry Corp (CNNC) analyst said on Tuesday.
"I think (exports) this year could reach 200,000 tonnes," Feng Juncong of CNNC's Techno-Economic Research Institute told Reuters.
Chinese officials have estimated 1995 lead and alloy exports at 150,000-180,000 tonnes.
Lead exports would remain relatively constant over the next few years, Feng said.
"Lead (exports)...are not very much influenced by prices," she said. "Exports are likely to be stable....(and) may remain at around 180,000 tonnes."
While exports were unlikely to fall sharply, they had only a limited capacity for growth in the short-term, she said.
"Export capacity is limited, it would be untenable to go beyond 200,000 tonnes," she said.

It was essential for China to boost the construction of lead mines and to make major efforts to develop lead regeneration and reform the lead mining and smelting industries, Feng said in a report to a metals conference in Beijing.
In the near future, China's lead mining would be characterised by numerous small ventures, meaning that large increases in lead concentrate output were unlikely, she said.
